premises.text: Home IoT devices are easy to hack because makers lack network security, exposing privacy and other devices on the home network
premises.evidence_span: the companies making those devices are clueless about intranet security

premises.text: Cujo is a plug-and-play smart gateway device that inventories every device on the home network
premises.evidence_span: Cujo is a little smart device, very powerful, that you connect to your network

premises.text: Cloud threat intelligence and device behavioral models block only anomalous device behavior while leaving devices working
premises.evidence_span: we also use machine learning to build behavioral models of your devices

premises.text: When one Cujo blocks a threat, other Cujos are updated in real time to block the same threat
premises.evidence_span: everyone else's Cujos are updated in real time and they can now block that same threat

premises.text: Product is sold as a hardware unit plus a monthly subscription for business-level protection of every network device
premises.evidence_span: Cujo is for sale for $99 as well as an $8.99 a month fee

domains.name: Cujo gateway and collective threat defense

value.text: Home networks and smart devices kept safe from remote cyber threats
value.evidence_span: the smart way to fight home hacking

causal_links.evidence_span: these same criminals are hacking your home and the smart devices
keep you safe against all kinds of cyber threats
keep every single device on your network protected on a business level

notes: Ransomware/webcam/stalking examples folded into one home-IoT threat premise (v1.5.1 §4.1.6). App inventory/block demo treated as cascade of the gateway mechanism; ML/cloud intelligence kept with gateway as the protection mechanism; real-time fleet update split as a separately failable network-effect condition. Unit sales traction excluded per §4.2; price+subscription kept as one commercial premise (§4.1.3). Singleton D1/D3 retained as independently revisable problem and monetization modules.
